new_theme: Build L1 (dev): the amplitude of a Rayleigh flat-fading channel. The open flowgraph is empty except for samp_rate = 48000. The user asks for complex Gaussian noise with RMS magnitude 0.8 (defined as sqrt(mean |z|^2)), its magnitude written as float samples to envelope.dat, and the R5 run sentence. The output must have RMS 0.8 and mean 0.709 (0.8*sqrt(pi)/2), each within 3 %. Reference: Noise Source (complex, amp 0.8) -> Throttle -> Complex to Mag -> File Sink. The knowledge tested is GNU Radio's complex amplitude convention: amp is the RMS magnitude, each component has amp/sqrt(2). v2 signature envelope|noise -> dev, cluster_id chain:envelope|noise. Distinct from gbf-test-03 (filter|noise, band-limited real noise) and gbf-dev-05 (noise|nonlinear, clipping of real noise, parameter-tune).
deviation_from_plan: (1) Tolerance 3 % instead of the plan's 2 %. My GNU Radio calibration (scratch d02_calib.py, 300 seeds, 65536-sample captures) found these spreads. The Noise Source stays within 0.62 %. The Fast Noise Source with its default 8192-variate pool spreads by sd 0.6 % (range -1.58..+1.86 %), and the Channel Model AWGN by sd 0.45 %. 2 % is therefore only about 3.3 sigma for a valid Fast Noise Source answer with a custom seed; 3 % is at least 5 sigma. 3 % still rejects the +5 % amplitude near miss (+4.6..+5.4 %), the per-component misreading (-29 %), the half-normal (-10 % mean) and uniform noise (-39 % mean). (2) Graph checks were added although the plan said none were needed. A rectified sine of RMS 0.8 meets both moments (mean +1.6 %), and the instruction says 'Generate complex Gaussian noise'. So a path check requires the File Sink to be fed from a noise generator: Noise Source, Fast Noise Source, or the AWGN of Channel Model, Channel Model 2 or Dynamic Channel Model. The stated 48 kHz is unobservable in white noise, so it is checked as a variable value (block_present variable 48000), per R4. (3) The plan's '|real noise| (Abs of float noise)' and 'amplitude 1.6' mutants are not single edits of the reference. The half-normal is probe half_normal (it fails P3). The amplitude mutants are the per-component misreading (amp 0.566) and a +5 % near miss (amp 0.84). (4) Seed 0, GNU Radio's default, turned out to be a fixed seed in 3.10.12, not time-seeded: 300 identical runs.

The lesson applies to the new mutant set: 6 mutants, each a different fault class with a different observed effect. Power instead of magnitude (mean 0.64, RMS 0.905); real part instead of magnitude (mean about 0); the per-component amplitude misreading (RMS -29 %); a +5 % amplitude near miss; uniform noise (mean -39 %); samp_rate 32000 (the P1 graph check). All 6 are killed.

The lesson applies: a moments-only oracle accepts deterministic shapes. Graph check P4 (a path from a noise generator to the File Sink) was added. Probe rectified_sine meets both moments and fails only this check. Probe fading_model_jakes (a sum-of-sinusoids Fading Model, not the noise the instruction asks for) also fails it.

The lesson applies: every number the new instruction states is checked. RMS 0.8 (rms, 3 %), mean 0.709 (mean, 3 %), 48 kHz (variable value), the file name and float type (observation point), and the run sentence (V4). 'Complex Gaussian noise' is checked by the P4 path plus the mean/RMS ratio (0.886): uniform and single-component noise fail, and GNU Radio's complex Laplacian and impulse types fail at run time. There are no unobservable design numbers such as filter edges or a gain split. The two remaining equivalences, a non-Gaussian source with the same two moments and a samp_rate written as an expression (probe samp_rate_expression), are recorded in review.notes.
